Current platforms depend on the Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA), which Shor's algorithm can break in polynomial time. This paper presents a statistically rigorous performance and security comparison of three NIST-standardized postquantum signature schemes-Dilithium2 (ML-DSA, FIPS 204), Falcon-512 (FN-DSA), and SPHINCS+ (SLH-DSA, FIPS 205)benchmarked against ECDSA in a blockchain context. Using the liboqs C library (version 0.11.0), we executed 1 000 benchmark iterations per algorithm and measured key-generation, signing, and verification latency together with signature and public-key sizes, reporting 95 % bootstrap confidence intervals throughout. Dilithium2 achieves the fastest signing (0.093 ms) and verification (0.030 ms) of all evaluated schemes. Falcon-512 offers the most compact post-quantum signatures (655 bytes) with verification at 0.058 ms. SPHINCS+ provides the strongest cryptographic assurance, but its signing latency of 799.7 ms and 7 856-byte signatures carry a significant overhead. A blockchain simulation assuming 1 000 transactions per block shows that Dilithium2 and Falcon-512 reach estimated cryptographic throughputs of 33 445 and 17 271 transactions per second (TPS) respectively-well above ECDSA's 1 303 TPS-while SPHINCS+ falls to 695 TPS. Based on these findings we map each algorithm to concrete deployment scenarios and outline a hybrid migration strategy for the transition to a post-quantum blockchain ecosystem."},{"DOI":"10.14357/08696527210404","title":["POST-QUANTUM SIGNATURE SCHEME ON MATRIX ALGEBRA"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2021,12,10]]},"container-title":["Systems and Means of Informatics"],"type":"journal-article"},{"DOI":"10.5220/0013508400003979","title":["Post-Quantum Digital Signature Algorithms on IoT: Evaluating Performance on LoRa ESP32 Microcontroller"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2025]]},"container-title":["Proceedings of the 22nd International Conference on Security and Cryptography"],"type":"proceedings-article"},{"DOI":"10.2139/ssrn.6492738","title":["PQ-Derived Schnorr: Post-Quantum Hybrid Signature Scheme for Bitcoin-Compatible Networks"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026]]},"type":"posted-content","abstract":"We present PQ-Derived Schnorr, a novel hybrid signature scheme that combines postquantum security with classical Bitcoin compatibility. Our approach leverages the CRYSTALS-Dilithium lattice-based signature scheme as the primary security foundation while maintaining full compatibility with existing Schnorr signature verification systems. The scheme implements a Dilithium First, Schnorr Derived philosophy, where the post-quantum component generates a challenge vector that serves as input to a classical Schnorr signature. This design ensures quantum resistance while preserving seamless integration with Bitcoin's Taproot and other Schnorr-based systems. While the total signature size is approximately 4.4 KB, the scheme is structurally optimized so that only a 64-byte Schnorr-compatible segment is required for verification on-chain in blockchain environments such as Bitcoin. Performance analysis shows signing times of 0.02-0.04 seconds, making it practical for real-world deployment. An advantage of using the secant variety of the Grassmannian is that it is defined by sparse cubic equations, which are in general more difficult to solve than quadratic ones, thereby reducing the size of the public key."},{"DOI":"10.21681/2311-3456-2024-4-65-70","title":["OPTIMIZATION OF COMPUTATIONS OVER POLYNOMIALS IN POST-QUANTUM SIGNATURE SCHEME"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2024]]},"container-title":["Voprosy kiberbezopasnosti"],"type":"journal-article"},{"DOI":"10.21203/rs.3.rs-5988828/v1","title":["Efficient Post-Quantum Digital Signature Schemes Using QC-MDPC"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2025,2,13]]},"type":"posted-content","abstract":"Abstract

With the development of quantum computers and quantum attack algorithms, it is crucial to design digital signature algorithms that are resistant to quantum attacks. CFS scheme is one of the most popular code-based digital signature schemes today, but it suffers from the disadvantages of large keys and low signature efficiency. To solve these problems, this paper proposes two post-quantum digital signature schemes based on Quasi-Cyclic Medium Density Parity Check Code (QC-MDPC). Both schemes are characterized by small public key storage, low encryption and decryption complexity, and high security, which are of great significance in the field of cryptographic research against quantum attacks.

In a multiparty setting, an initial adaptor signature allows each party create additional adaptor signatures without the original secret. Adaptor signatures help address scalability and interoperabity issues in blockchain. They can also bring some important advantages to cryptocurrencies, such as low on-chain cost, improved transaction fungibility, and less limitations of a blockchain’s scripting language. In this paper, we propose a new two-party adaptor signature scheme that relies on quantum-safe hard problems in coding theory. The proposed scheme uses a hash-and-sign code-based signature scheme introduced by Debris-Alazard et al. and a code-based hard relation defined from the well-known syndrome decoding problem. To achieve all the basic properties of adaptor signatures formalized by Aumayr et al., we introduce further modifications to the aforementioned signature scheme. We also give a security analysis of our scheme and its application to the atomic swap. After providing a set of parameters for our scheme, we show that it has the smallest pre-signature size compared to existing post-quantum adaptor signatures."},{"DOI":"10.1007/s12046-026-03281-8","title":["Cryptanalysis of post-quantum linkable ring signature schemes"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,12]]},"container-title":["Sādhanā"],"type":"journal-article"},{"DOI":"10.52190/2073-2600_2021_3_40","title":["Post-quantum digital signature algorithm on commutative algebra"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2021]]},"container-title":["Information Security Questions"],"type":"journal-article"},{"DOI":"10.5220/0002070100870096","title":["Fourier Signature in Log-Polar Images"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2007]]},"container-title":["Robot Vision"],"type":"proceedings-article"},{"DOI":"10.21203/rs.3.rs-10018675/v1","title":["HashGuard-FL: Learnable Hash-Based GAN Discriminator with Post-Quantum Audit Trail for Federated Learning Integrity"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026,7,9]]},"type":"posted-content","abstract":"Abstract

Federated learning (FL) deployments in safety-critical domains face two entangled integrity problems: (i) detecting adversarial model updates at runtime, and (ii) producing a long-lived, tamper-evident audit trail whose authenticity must survive post-quantum cryptanalysis. Existing Byzantine-robust aggregation rules, gradient anomaly detectors, and cryptographic provenance schemes each address one dimension but none provides an integrated solution that achieves fine-grained multi-class detection, non-IID robustness, and quantum-resistant auditability simultaneously. We propose HashGuard-FL, a framework that couples a learnable hash-based GAN discriminator with a post-quantum audit layer built on SHAKE-256 transcripts and ML-DSA-65 (CRYSTALS-Dilithium, NIST FIPS-204) signatures. The discriminator projects each client update into a compact 128-bit locality-sensitive hash space and learns, via adversarial and contrastive training, a decision boundary separating five operationally defined attack classes (C0-C4: benign, poisoned, unstable, replayed, and tampered) without sharing raw gradients. The audit layer commits every round decision to an append-only, BQP-hard verifiable transcript. Across four benchmarks (MNIST, CIFAR-10, FEMNIST, PTB-XL ECG), HashGuard-FL achieves macro-F1 of 0.962 and AUROC of 0.989, outperforming eight baselines by up to 0.111 F1 points while adding only 2.3 ms per-round overhead. A clinical simulation over 500 rounds confirms sustained accuracy and a stable FPR of 0.034 under adaptive adversaries.

"},{"DOI":"10.3390/app112411974","title":["Efficient Online Log Parsing with Log Punctuations Signature"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2021,12,16]]},"container-title":["Applied Sciences"],"type":"journal-article","abstract":"Logs, recording the system runtime information, are frequently used to ensure software system reliability. As the first and foremost step of typical log analysis, many data-driven methods have been proposed for automated log parsing. Most existing log parsers work offline, requiring a time-consuming training progress and retraining as the system upgrades. Meanwhile, the state of the art online log parsers are tree-based, which still have defects in robustness and efficiency. To overcome such limitations, we abandon the tree structure and propose a hash-like method. In this paper, we propose LogPunk, an efficient online log parsing method. The core of LogPunk is a novel log signature method based on log punctuations and length features. According to the signature, we can quickly find a small set of candidate templates. Further, the most suitable template is returned by traversing the candidate set with our log similarity function. We evaluated LogPunk on 16 public datasets from the LogHub comparing with five other log parsers. LogPunk achieves the best parsing accuracy of 91.9%. Evaluation results also demonstrate its superiority in terms of robustness and efficiency."},{"DOI":"10.2139/ssrn.7524468","title":["PQCAF: A Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption Framework for Compliance-Oriented Deployment and Audit"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026]]},"type":"posted-content","abstract":"Quantum computing appears to resolve the complex processes in very fast and efficient manner, which lead to its high adoption in different sectors world wide. Therefore, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) finalized three post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards in 2024: ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205). These standards provide the algorithmic foundation for quantum resistant systems. Existing policy documents provide strategic intent without verifiable audit criteria; benchmarking studies characterize performance without connecting findings to compliance requirements. This paper introduces the Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption Framework (PQCAF). PQCAF is built on a systematic gap analysis of four international frameworks-NIST FIPS 203-205, ISO/IEC 14888-3:2023, ENISA PQC Roadmap 2025, and NSA-CISA-NIST joint guidance-revealing that no single framework provides complete coverage across five proposed readiness dimensions, and that two dimensions (resource sensitivity and cross-jurisdictional policy convergence) receive no measurable treatment from any current standard. The proposed framework, can be used pre-assessment stage or post-implementation stage to ensure the compliance with the international governance an standards. The selected indicators in this research from different standards mapped with audit requirements and provided and governance roadmap."},{"DOI":"10.52190/2073-2600_2023_2_54","title":["Post-quantum digital signature algorithm with doubled verification equation"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2023]]},"container-title":["Information Security Questions"],"type":"journal-article"}],"items-per-page":25,"query":{"start-index":0,"search-terms":null}}}
